title: ISTQB Foundation Level Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of ISTQB Foundation Level concepts

questions.text: What is the main purpose of testing?

choices.text: To find defects and reduce the level of risk of poor software quality
choices.explanation: This is the correct answer because testing's primary purpose is to identify defects early and minimize risks. Testing helps ensure software quality by finding issues before they reach production, thus reducing the risk of software failures.

choices.text: To make software that works perfectly
choices.explanation: This is incorrect because achieving 'perfect' software is practically impossible. Testing helps improve software quality but cannot guarantee perfection.

choices.text: To prove that all defects have been fixed
choices.explanation: This is incorrect because testing cannot prove the absence of defects. It can only show their presence and help reduce their occurrence.

choices.text: To ensure that the software is 100% bug-free
choices.explanation: This is incorrect because achieving 100% bug-free software is impossible. Testing helps identify and fix bugs but cannot guarantee their complete absence.

keyPoints: Testing is about finding defects and reducing risks
Perfect or bug-free software is an unrealistic goal
Testing shows the presence of defects, not their absence
Risk reduction is a key aspect of testing

questions.text: Which of the following is a test level?

choices.explanation: Integration testing is indeed a test level. Test levels are specific phases in the testing process that deal with particular testing objectives. Other test levels include unit testing, system testing, and acceptance testing.
White box testing is a test technique, not a test level. It refers to testing with knowledge of the internal code structure, but doesn't define when in the development process testing occurs.
Exploratory testing is a testing approach or technique, not a test level. It involves simultaneous learning, test design, and test execution.
Regression testing is a type of testing, not a test level. It focuses on retesting after changes to ensure existing functionality still works.

keyPoints: Test levels are distinct phases in the testing process
Main test levels are: unit, integration, system, and acceptance testing
Test techniques (like white-box) and types (like regression) are different from test levels
Each test level has specific objectives and scope

questions.text: What is the difference between verification and validation?

choices.text: Verification: Are we building the product right? Validation: Are we building the right product?
choices.explanation: This distinction is fundamental in software quality assurance. Verification focuses on checking if the product meets specified requirements (building it right), while validation ensures the product meets user needs (building the right thing).

This is incorrect. While both are quality assurance activities, they have distinct purposes. Verification checks conformance to specifications, while validation checks if the product meets user needs.

choices.text: Verification is done by developers, validation by testers
choices.explanation: This is incorrect. The distinction is not about who performs the activity, but rather what is being checked. Both developers and testers can perform both verification and validation activities.

choices.text: Verification is manual testing, validation is automated testing
choices.explanation: This is incorrect. The distinction is not about how the testing is performed (manually or automated). Both verification and validation can use either manual or automated approaches.

keyPoints: Verification focuses on meeting specifications ('building it right')
Validation focuses on meeting user needs ('building the right thing')
Both activities can be performed by any team member
Both can use manual or automated approaches
